body: claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-16T13:41Z · worktree/branch issue/2176-custom-holder-sim · plan: trace the holder shape of each consumer, report it here, then make the simulation body read the same shape as the checks

Trace of the holder shape for a tool with a custom (drawn) holder profile. This is the first step of the work.

The drawn profile lands as one `ToolBody` on the tool entity (`crates/app/src/tool_body.rs`, `build_spun`). The body holds the `SpunProfile` and `BodyFrame::Spindle { profile }`, where `profile = SpunProfile::holder_profile()` (the bands of the drawn outline, `crates/tools/src/spun.rs`). The parametric fields (`holder_d`, `holder_len`) stay on the `Tool` record.

Which shape each consumer reads:

1. Viewport simulation body: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/world.rs` `sim_tool_tris` -> `SimToolCache::posed` -> `sim_tool_body::for_operation` (`crates/app/src/sim_tool_body.rs`). It calls `tool_body::judged` and `tool_body::stack`, then draws the holder bands as cylinders (`JudgedOutline::holder_meridian`). It does not draw the drawn outline. A taper or an arc becomes a cylinder at its larger radius. This is the "stacked cylinders" in the screenshot.
2. Collision checks: `operation/tool_gate.rs` `job_tool` -> `tool_body::judged`; `operation/generate.rs` and `generate/run_job.rs` -> `tool_body::stack` + `verify::Cutter::with_body`; `fixture_struck.rs` -> `judged` + `stack`; `machine/mod.rs` and `posting_index_swing.rs` -> `judged`. All read the bands of the drawn profile, or the cylinder that encloses them (`HolderProfile::enclose`, `operation/body_judged.rs` `falls_back`). The enclosing cylinder is never smaller than the bands.
3. Verify step that can block the post: `posting_sim.rs` -> `operation/kept_rejudge.rs` `moved_part_problem` -> `collect_job` -> `job_tool` -> `tool_body::judged` + `tool_body::stack`. The same bands. The op stamp (`tool_body::digest`) hashes these bands, so a profile edit makes the op stale.
4. Profile preview in the tool editor: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` `profile_section` -> `tool_body_view::spun_preview` on the editor draft points, drawn with `SpunProfile::outline()`. This is the exact drawn outline (arcs flattened outward).

Result: no check reads the parametric fields while a drawn profile is set. The checks read the bands of the drawn profile. Each band is never smaller than the drawn outline at its height (`SpunProfile::bands`, conservative by construction). Thus a holder collision cannot pass because of this defect. The priority stays `P3`.

The defect is display only: the simulation draws the bands, not the drawn outline. The fix makes the simulation draw the outline of the same landed `SpunProfile` that the checks read the bands of. The checks do not change.
